draft.title: A training session
card: Warm up
the first phase, using light activity that slowly raises heart rate and muscle temperature. It often includes dynamic stretches and drills like those in the sport to come.
Conditioning
the main phase, where the training goal is worked on. This is where the fitness component is trained, such as endurance, speed or strength.
Cool down
the last phase, using light activity that slowly lowers heart rate and breathing. It helps the body return towards its resting state.
Each phase has its own job. A session that leaves out the warm up or cool down misses what that phase offers.
draft.remember: Warm up prepares the body, conditioning trains it, cool down brings it back to rest.

a.q: Which activity belongs in the conditioning phase of a session?
opts: Work aimed at the fitness goal of the session
Light jogging to raise muscle temperature
Slow walking to bring heart rate down
Dynamic drills that copy the movements of the sport
a.why: The conditioning phase is the main part, where the training goal is worked on. Light jogging and dynamic drills prepare the body, so they belong in the warm up. Slow walking belongs in the cool down.
a.clue: Which phase is the main one, where the goal is trained?

b.q: Priya, a netballer in Geelong, finishes a hard sprint session and sits down straight away. Which phase has she left out?
opts: The cool down, which lowers heart rate gradually
The warm up, which raises muscle temperature
The conditioning phase, which trains the goal
The warm up, which lowers heart rate gradually
b.why: She went from hard work to sitting, so she skipped the cool down. The cool down uses light activity to bring heart rate down slowly. The warm up comes at the start of a session, so it cannot be the missing phase here.
b.clue: Look at what happened at the end of the session.

a.best: Work aimed at the fitness goal of the session

b.best: The cool down, which lowers heart rate gradually
